speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: asked	the Minister for National Development (a) what are the plans for HDB commercial shops that have their 30-year lease expiring in a few years; and (b) what are the long-term plans for towns with these commercial shops not partaking in the Revitalisation of Shops (ROS) scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: HDB shops are an integral part of public housing estates and are provided to meet residents' needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Revitalisation of Shops or ROS scheme has been designed specifically for HDB shops, to help enhance their vibrancy and improve their competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Under this scheme, the Local Merchants' Associations have the opportunity to lead and drive the revitalisation of their respective shop clusters, with funding support from the Town Council and HDB.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides the ROS scheme, HDB has other programmes to rejuvenate older towns and estates, like the Remaking Our Heartland (ROH) programme, which provides enhancements for the entire town.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: First, for those where the tenure is already up, how long will the lease be for the renewal?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Second, what are the criteria under MND for the mix of those on sale and of the lease of the shops?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Last, would MND consider the transfer of ownership between one generation and the other, if we want to have some businesses thrive over generations?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There was a certain point in time when these were put out on a "sold" basis to encourage ownership, but this is not the case today.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On transfer of business from generation to generation, I presume Miss Chan is referring to sold shops and whether those can be transferred from one generation to the next.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, if it is within the period where it is owned by that person and he wants to pass it on to the children, that could be considered.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If it goes beyond that particular tenure, then that is a separate matter which would have to be considered separately.
